On Tue, 24 Feb 2026 at 15:03, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Following up on our MAP — wanted to lock in this week's checkpoint to run through the latest perf numbers and align on close timeline implications.

Thanks Rishi — I ran the batch from last week's job matrix and attached the raw CSV. TL;DR: we see consistent p50 but p95 spikes on long-tail contexts when KV cache misses occur. Key numbers from the 1M-token sample (default config):

- p50 generation (8-token response): ~120ms
- p95 generation (8-token response): ~520ms (long-tail at ~1% of requests)
- Sustained throughput on the test rig (A100s, 16GB): ~1,100 tok/s per GPU at batch size 8
- With prefix caching enabled for common prompts, p95 improves to ~380ms (cache hit rate ~46%)

Notes / hypotheses:
- The dominant tail factor is KV cache eviction strategy on mixed-length sessions; tuning the cache admission policy + slightly larger kv-cache allocation reduces p95 with minimal cost uptick.
- Quantization profile B (int8+remap) reduces per-token compute ~22% in our tests but increases p95 variance on very long sequences; we should test with the combination of prefix caching + profile B for a balanced result.

Attachments: perf_q1_summary.csv, kv_cache_experiments.pdf

I'll bring a short deck to the checkpoint with plots.

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Monica Patel: produce pricing delta for Dedicated capacity vs hosted: include incremental cost for the higher kv allocation + quantization licensing note by 2026-03-04.
- Marissa Cole: draft canary playbook + rollback SOP; include monitoring checks (p95, error-rate, trailing token diff) and runbook for immediate rollback by 2026-03-06.
- Rishi Malhotra: update MAP timeline & schedule canary window (target week of 2026-03-09); coordinate procurement steps with Acme and provide updated MAP by 2026-03-03.

Acceptance criteria for canary (agreed):
- p95 <= 450ms on production prompt set (measured over 24-hour window)
- Customer-facing error rate < 0.2%
- Cost delta <= 12% vs current baseline (Monica to confirm)
